title: Context-quality regression triage
summary: This intermediate resource answers whether the requested correction can be applied safely. It cannot be applied until the existing guide, changed citation, affected claims, and authoritative triage procedure are available.
prerequisites: The verbatim current contents of the resource being corrected
The complete existing citation record and its current first-party location
Authoritative material supporting the existing triage procedure and verification criteria

sections.title: Immediate answer
paragraphs: Can a practitioner safely use this correction to triage a context-quality regression? No. The existing guide and an approved definition of context-quality regression were not supplied, so its diagnostic procedure, decision points, recovery actions, and success criteria are UNKNOWN and omitted.

Do not infer a procedure from the resource name. Obtain the current resource and its supporting material first. If they cannot be obtained, stop the correction and request them from the repository maintainer rather than replacing reviewed material with unsupported instructions.

sections.title: Correction status
paragraphs: Which cited source changed is UNKNOWN. The supplied citation record identifies only an unregistered publisher and says the source was never verified. It does not provide a title, former URL, replacement URL, review date, or the claims the source supports.

What the citation change affected is also UNKNOWN. If the complete citation record becomes available, verify its current first-party HTTPS location and identify every claim that depends on it. If the location cannot be verified, retain no unsupported replacement claim and request retrieved source material with provenance.

Material unaffected by the change cannot be identified because the baseline resource was not supplied. If the baseline remains unavailable, do not commit a purported correction. RFC 8259 establishes JSON syntax, but it does not supply the missing resource content, catalogue history, or subject-matter procedure.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence consists of the verbatim baseline resource pinned to a repository revision, the complete former source entry, the source's verified current first-party HTTPS location, a mapping from that source to the affected claims, and authoritative support for each retained triage instruction and remediation.

Verify the correction by comparing it with the pinned baseline. Only the identified source record and the claims demonstrably affected by that source may differ. Confirm that all other metadata and guide text are unchanged, that the resource still has exactly three sections, and that every procedure step that can fail names a next action.

If any expected evidence is missing or the comparison reveals unrelated edits, verification fails. Restore the unrelated material from the baseline and repeat the comparison. If the baseline or claim mapping cannot be recovered, leave the correction blocked rather than asserting completion.
